newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-PRESIDENT HAS NOT MADE UP HIS MIND-SPOKESMAN.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-PRESIDENT HAS NOT MADE UP HIS MIND-SPOKESMAN.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas has made no firm decision yet about his political future and will not announce his intentions before early October, the president's office said on Monday.
"The president will announce his decision at the beginning of October as required by the presidential election law," the sopkesman for the president's office, Jonas Rekeshius, said.
The Estonian newspaper Sonumileht reported on Monday that Brazauskas, 64, was considering not running for a second term of office in December's presidential race.
In an interview with the paper, Brazauskas cited his age and political past as factors leading him to consider calling it quits. But he added that he had not made up his mind yet.
"I think it's enough. First off all there is my age," Brazauskas was quoted by the paper as saying.

"I also look critically at my political biography...I was the first secretary of the Lithuania's Communist Party...but where in Europe is there such a president left? I am the only one left," he was quoted as saying.
Rekeshius said that the interview was not the last word.
"The opinion which was expressed in not necessarily the final decision," Rekeshius said.
If Brazauskas does decide to run, he will face his arch-political rival Vytautas Landsbergis, who is currently chairman of parliament.
